- scripts/review_findings_record.py:63-269 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9._:-]+$")` (line 63) keeps a FLAGGED_BY entry only if it has the `vendor/model` shape. That check runs in `parse_review_issues().finish()` (lines 257-269). But `scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh` `load_known_reviewers()`/`sanitize_flagged_by()` (lines 378-431) only emits reviewer safe-names (file basenames such as `review_anthropic_claude-opus-5`) or `reviewer_N` tokens, and none of those contain "/". So every real attribution is dropped into `flagged_by_dropped`.
  WHY: In production, every issue's `flagged_by` ends up as `[]` or `["unknown"]`, which defeats the per-slot comparison the trial exists for. Tests pass only because the fixture uses `chatgpt/gpt-6-sol, anthropic/claude-opus-5`, a shape the parser never emits. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and minimax_minimax-m3 said BLOCKER; google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash said MAJOR. The highest (BLOCKER→critical) is used.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4044-4060 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `build_record` reads `AUTOFIX_ITERATION_METRIC` to set `round` (scripts/review_findings_record.py:459). The new "Write review findings record" step's env block (lines 4047-4050) does not map that variable. It is set only in a later step's env (review_autofix.yml:6026) and is never exported to GITHUB_ENV.
  WHY: `record["round"]` is always null in production, and no warning is raised because `_identity_field` only warns on a non-empty raw value. The fixture's `AUTOFIX_ITERATION_METRIC="3"` hides this. Suggested fix: add `AUTOFIX_ITERATION_METRIC: ${{ steps.retrigger_guard.outputs.autofix_iteration || '' }}` to the step env.
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:56-473 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$")` is applied to the tier reason via `_token(tier_reason_raw, TOKEN_RE)` in `build_record` (~lines 470-473). It rejects `<` and `=`, which appear in every lite/standard tier reason set in scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:2026-2037 (e.g. `doc_only_<=${lite_loc}_loc`, `code_<=${standard_loc}_loc`).
  WHY: On every lite/standard-tier round, `tier.reason` is null and `invalid_tier_reason` is added. That flips the outcome to `partial` and emits a ::warning:: on a healthy run. The fixture's `REVIEW_TIER_REASON: "default"` hides this.

- scripts/review_findings_record.py:build_record() record["consolidator"] | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: `"ran": issues_text is not None` is true whenever the issues file exists. But scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh `finish_parse_failure()` (line 52) and line 907, and scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh line 1078, truncate REVIEW_ISSUES_FILE to empty when parsing fails or is skipped.
